financials_interim.notes: COMPANY (standalone) basis, same filing/period as GROUP row -- see GROUP row's notes for shared context (TAP-GREG ownership finding, no printed Operating Profit subtotal). Company revenue (Rs.10.656mn, all Gross Profit, no Direct Cost/COGS line) is negligible next to Group's Rs.4,761.585mn -- consistent with TAP being a pure investment holding entity at standalone level; virtually all of Group revenue sits in subsidiaries. operating_profit computed as GP+Other Income-Admin Expenses+FV change (no SD expense line at Company level, no equity-accounted investee at Company level, consistent with the GREG-style 'Operating Profit' definition since there is no segment-note subtotal at Company level for TAP): 2026 = 10.656+0.260-7.654+164.054 = 167.316mn; 2025 = 0+66.939-13.935+131.996 = 185.000mn (2025 Company revenue was nil/dash, i.e. Rs.0). Company FV gain (+Rs.164.054mn, 2026) moves in the OPPOSITE direction to Group's FV LOSS (-Rs.238.179mn) -- these are genuinely different pools: Company's FVTPL book is Rs.4,467.906mn (its own direct quoted-equity holdings, per Note 8) vs Group's consolidated Rs.15,742.868mn (includes subsidiaries' larger and differently-composed portfolios, predominantly held within the Financial Services segment) -- not an extraction error. Company Other Income fell ~100% YoY (Rs.0.260mn vs Rs.66.939mn 2025) -- 2025's figure was almost entirely dividend income per the cash flow statement (Script/Cash Dividend Income Rs.57.605mn, Company, 2025) which was much smaller in 2026 (dividend income shown only at Group level in 2026's cash flow, Rs.350.034mn, not separately at Company level this period -- a genuine period-to-period difference in dividend upstreaming, not necessarily disclosed as a 'gap' since the cash flow simply shows no Company-level dividend line item in 2026). Company swung from PBT +Rs.54.123mn (2025) to -Rs.25.003mn (2026) -- Admin expenses fell 45% (Rs.7.654mn vs Rs.13.935mn) and Finance Cost rose 47% (Rs.192.319mn vs Rs.130.878mn); the swing is driven primarily by the Rs.66.679mn YoY drop in Other Income, only partly offset by the Rs.32.058mn YoY increase in FV gain. shares_in_issue = 1,022,352,863, same register as Group (Company is the parent entity's own share count). EPS cross-check: -25,003,284 / 1,022,352,863 = -0.02446 -> -0.02, ties. Identity check: total_liabilities (1,734.313+5,644.097=7,378.410) + total_equity (9,484.887) = 16,863.297 ~ printed Total Assets 16,863.296mn, ties (rounding).

Ambeon Capital PLC (TAP), investment holding/managing company, FYE 31 March. GROUP (consolidated) basis. Q1 FY2026/27 (period ended 30 June 2026) vs Q1 FY2025/26 (period ended 30 June 2025) comparative, both presented as single 'For the Period Ended 30th June' columns on the face P&L (page 3) -- since this is the FIRST quarter of TAP's fiscal year (FYE 31 March), the 3-month and cumulative-YTD figures are identical, so no QoQ distinction applies. IMPORTANT OWNERSHIP FINDING (corrects an assumption in the task brief): TAP is NOT a subsidiary/related entity of Ambeon Holdings PLC (GREG) -- the reverse holds. Per GREG's Note 4.4 (Twenty Major Shareholders, page 8), Ambeon Capital PLC (TAP) itself, directly plus via four bank-collateral accounts held in its name (Seylan/Commercial/DFCC/Pan Asia), holds 81.43% of GREG's ordinary shares. TAP's own top shareholder (Note 4.4, page 9) is 'Ambeon Consolidated (Private) Limited' at 50.16% -- a private entity, not GREG. So TAP is GREG's majority PARENT, not its subsidiary or peer. TAP's Group accounts therefore consolidate GREG (81.43% owned, hence the NCI line) PLUS TAP's own directly-held subsidiaries that sit OUTSIDE GREG's own consolidation perimeter -- notably Ambeon Essentials (Private) Limited / Harischandra Mills PLC (Note 9: 51.11% stake acquired 14 May 2026 for Rs.3,335.801mn consideration, generating goodwill of Rs.2,329.811mn), which appears in TAP's segment note as the new 'Manufacturing' segment but has NO equivalent line in GREG's own segment note (confirming it sits directly under TAP, not under GREG). The 'IT and Related Services' segment (~Rs.3,059.95mn revenue, ~64% of TAP Group revenue) and 'Financial Services'/'Property'/'Investment' segment figures are near-identical between the two filings' segment notes, confirming these sit within GREG and flow up into TAP's consolidated numbers as expected given the 81.43% ownership. P&L STRUCTURE CAVEAT: unlike GREG's filing, TAP's face P&L (page 3) prints NO separate 'Operating Profit' subtotal -- Change in Fair Value of FVTPL financial assets flows directly into a line immediately before Finance Cost and PBT. operating_profit is therefore taken from TAP's own segmental note (Note 2, page 8) 'Profit/(Loss) Before Net Finance Cost', Group Total column: 2026 (101,556) th = -101.556mn (verified: PBT -511,491 + Finance Cost 409,935 = -101,556, ties exactly since Share of Equity Accounted Investee = 0 in 2026); 2025 = 1,074,090 th = 1,074.090mn (this figure NETS a Rs.35,792th/-35.792mn Share of Results of Equity Accounted Investee loss, since the segment note computes 'before net finance cost' after that line -- verified via GP 891,005+OI 151,330-SD 65,769-Admin 547,888+FV gain 681,203 = 1,109,881, less the 35,792 investee loss = 1,074,089~1,074,090, reconciles). This differs slightly from how GREG's own filing defines its printed 'Operating Profit' line (GREG's is computed BEFORE the equity-investee line even for the comparative period) -- flagged so the two entities' operating_profit fields are not perfectly like-for-like subtotal definitions, both still approximate pre-finance-cost operating performance. REVENUE DRIVER: Group revenue +21% YoY to Rs.4,761.585mn (2025: Rs.3,919.061mn) driven entirely by the new Manufacturing segment (Harischandra Mills, footwear), which contributed Rs.1,377.435mn in this quarter with a '-' (nil) 2025 comparator since the acquisition only completed 14 May 2026 -- i.e. more than 100% of the Rs.842.524mn YoY revenue increase came from this single newly-consolidated segment, while legacy segments were mixed: IT and Related Services (largest legacy segment) revenue fell 8.5% (Rs.3,059.950mn vs Rs.3,344.821mn), Financial Services fell 63.4% (Rs.149.931mn vs Rs.410.081mn), Property/Investment fell 1.3% (Rs.152.050mn vs Rs.154.085mn), while IT & Related Services' small sibling category rose (Rs.22.219mn vs Rs.10.074mn, +121%). PROFIT DRIVER: despite revenue growth, Group swung from PBT +Rs.803.005mn (2025) to PBT -Rs.511.491mn (2026), a swing of Rs.1,314.496mn. The single largest driver is the 'Change in Fair Value of Financial Assets measured at FVTPL' line, which swung from a Rs.681.203mn GAIN (2025) to a Rs.238.179mn LOSS (2026) -- a Rs.919.382mn negative swing, i.e. ~70% of the total PBT swing, entirely a mark-to-market movement on the Group's quoted-equity FVTPL book (Rs.15,742.868mn at 30 June 2026 per Note 8) tied to broader market pricing, not an operating/trading item. Gross margin also compressed on an operating basis: Direct Cost rose 33% (Rs.4,020.213mn vs Rs.3,028.056mn) faster than revenue's 21% growth, so Group gross margin fell from 22.7% (891.005/3919.061) to 15.6% (741.371/4761.585) -- consistent with the newly-consolidated Manufacturing segment carrying a structurally lower/different margin profile than the legacy IT/Financial Services mix. Finance costs also rose 51% YoY to Rs.409.935mn (2025: Rs.271.085mn), adding further pressure, plausibly reflecting acquisition-related and NCI-funding debt (non-current interest-bearing borrowings rose from Rs.1,906.996mn at 31-Mar-26 to Rs.3,351.252mn at 30-Jun-26). Tax expense fell 42% YoY (Rs.41.830mn vs Rs.71.991mn) -- a mechanical consequence of the swing to a group loss, not a rate improvement. BALANCE SHEET: total_liabilities computed as Non-Current (4,375.852) + Current (21,821.161) = 26,197.013mn -- this is Rs.1th off the segment note's own printed Group Total Liabilities of 26,197,012th (26,197.012mn), an immaterial rounding difference; segment note's own figure used where a direct choice was needed elsewhere. trade_payables = 'Trade and Other Payables' (5,773.634mn) as printed, a combined line, no separate pure-trade breakdown disclosed. cash_from_investing (2,004.123mn, a NET INFLOW despite the line being labelled 'Net Cash Flow Used in Investing Activities') and capex (180.447mn, 'Acquisition of Property, Plant & Equipment', gross, not netted against the Rs.18.806mn of disposal proceeds) taken as printed. shares_in_issue = 1,022,352,863 (Note 4.1). EPS cross-check: Group -395,129,713 (Note 5 numerator, exact rupees) / 1,022,352,863 = -0.3865 -> -0.39, ties printed EPS. Identity check: total_liabilities (26,197.013) + total_equity (13,156.445) = 39,353.458 ~ printed Total Assets 39,353.457mn, ties (rounding).

interim_updates.note_text: Ambeon Capital PLC (TAP), investment holding/managing company (Group segments: Manufacturing/footwear, Investment, Property, IT and Related Services, Financial Services), reported a Group net loss of Rs.553.321mn for Q1 FY2026/27 (period ended 30 June 2026), reversing a Rs.731.014mn profit in Q1 FY2025/26 (period ended 30 June 2025). Group revenue rose 21% YoY to Rs.4,761.585mn (2025: Rs.3,919.061mn), driven entirely by the newly-consolidated Manufacturing segment (Harischandra Mills PLC, footwear -- 51.11% stake acquired 14 May 2026 for Rs.3,335.801mn consideration, Note 9), which alone contributed Rs.1,377.435mn of revenue this quarter against a nil 2025 comparator -- more than 100% of the Rs.842.524mn total revenue increase, since the largest legacy segment, IT and Related Services, actually fell 8.5% YoY to Rs.3,059.950mn (2025: Rs.3,344.821mn) and Financial Services fell 63.4% to Rs.149.931mn (2025: Rs.410.081mn). Despite revenue growth, Group PBT swung from +Rs.803.005mn to -Rs.511.491mn (a Rs.1,314.496mn swing), driven primarily by 'Change in Fair Value of Financial Assets measured at FVTPL' swinging from a Rs.681.203mn unrealised GAIN (2025) to a Rs.238.179mn unrealised LOSS (2026) -- a Rs.919.382mn negative swing that alone explains ~70% of the total PBT movement, a mark-to-market item on the Group's Rs.15,742.868mn FVTPL quoted-equity book, not an operating/trading item. Gross margin also compressed on an operating basis, from 22.7% to 15.6%, as Direct Cost rose 33% (faster than revenue's 21% growth) -- consistent with the newly-added Manufacturing segment's different cost structure. Finance costs rose 51% YoY to Rs.409.935mn (2025: Rs.271.085mn). CORRECTION TO AN ASSUMPTION IN THE TASK BRIEF: TAP is NOT a subsidiary/related entity of Ambeon Holdings PLC (GREG) as originally framed; the reverse holds -- TAP itself (directly, plus via four bank-collateral holding accounts) owns 81.43% of GREG per GREG's own Note 4.4 shareholder register, making TAP the majority PARENT of GREG, while TAP's own majority shareholder is the separate private entity 'Ambeon Consolidated (Private) Limited' (50.16%). TAP's Group accounts therefore consolidate GREG (hence the Rs.158.191mn NCI loss this quarter) plus TAP's own directly-held Harischandra Mills acquisition, which sits OUTSIDE GREG's own consolidation perimeter (confirmed by GREG's own segment note showing no Manufacturing/Footwear segment).
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to 30 June 2026 has been collected for TAP -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. TAP's own segment note (Note 2) 'Results' row (profit before net finance cost) could not be reliably mapped column-by-column to the Footwear/Manufacturing/Investment/Property/IT/Financial Services headers for the 2025 comparative (apparent column-count mismatch vs the Revenue row -- a formatting artifact in the source filing itself), so segment-level PBT attribution was NOT used in this narrative; only segment REVENUE (which reconciles exactly to the Group Total in both years) was cited as a driver. TAP discloses no separate Finance Income line (only Finance Cost) -- finance_income left blank. Company-level segment information is not disclosed at all (the segment note is Group-only).
interim_updates.takeaway: TAP's Q1 FY2026/27 headline swing from a Rs.731.014mn Group profit to a Rs.553.321mn Group loss was overwhelmingly a mark-to-market story, not an operating collapse: a Rs.919.382mn negative swing in unrealised fair value on the Group's Rs.15,742.868mn FVTPL quoted-equity book explains roughly 70% of the Rs.1,314.496mn PBT deterioration. Underlying revenue actually grew 21% to Rs.4,761.585mn, but entirely because of the first-time consolidation of Harischandra Mills PLC (footwear, Rs.1,377.435mn revenue, 51.11% stake acquired 14 May 2026) -- the legacy IT and Related Services (-8.5%) and Financial Services (-63.4%) segments both shrank, and Direct Cost grew faster than revenue (33% vs 21%), compressing gross margin from 22.7% to 15.6%. Investors should also note TAP is the 81.43%-majority PARENT of Ambeon Holdings PLC (GREG), not the reverse -- TAP's Group figures consolidate GREG plus the newly-acquired Harischandra Mills, which sits outside GREG's own accounts.

yoy.label: Operating Profit (Group, before net finance cost)

operational_highlights: Group Revenue Rs.4,761.585mn, +21% YoY (2025: Rs.3,919.061mn); Group operating loss (profit before net finance cost, per segment note) Rs.101.556mn vs a Rs.1,074.090mn profit in 2025; Group PAT -Rs.553.321mn vs +Rs.731.014mn in 2025.

Manufacturing segment (Harischandra Mills, footwear, 51.11% stake acquired 14 May 2026) contributed Rs.1,377.435mn revenue this quarter (2025: nil) -- more than the entire Rs.842.524mn YoY revenue increase, since IT and Related Services (-8.5% to Rs.3,059.950mn) and Financial Services (-63.4% to Rs.149.931mn) both declined.

Change in Fair Value of FVTPL financial assets swung Rs.919.382mn negative YoY, from a Rs.681.203mn gain (2025) to a Rs.238.179mn loss (2026), on a Rs.15,742.868mn Group FVTPL book -- the single largest driver of the swing to a Group loss.

Gross margin compressed from 22.7% to 15.6% as Direct Cost rose 33% (Rs.4,020.213mn vs Rs.3,028.056mn), faster than revenue's 21% growth; Finance Cost rose 51% YoY to Rs.409.935mn (2025: Rs.271.085mn).

Company (standalone) basis swung from PBT +Rs.54.123mn to -Rs.25.003mn, driven by Other Income falling from Rs.66.939mn to Rs.0.260mn, only partly offset by a Rs.164.054mn FV gain (2025: Rs.131.996mn) on the Company's own Rs.4,467.906mn FVTPL portfolio -- moving in the OPPOSITE direction to the Group's FV loss since these are different asset pools.
key_drivers: Fair value swing on Group FVTPL financial assets: -Rs.238.179mn loss (2026) vs +Rs.681.203mn gain (2025), a Rs.919.382mn negative swing = ~70% of the total Rs.1,314.496mn PBT deterioration -- unrealised, on a Rs.15,742.868mn quoted-equity book, not a trading/operating driver.

First-time consolidation of Harischandra Mills PLC (footwear, 51.11% stake, acquired 14 May 2026 for Rs.3,335.801mn) added Rs.1,377.435mn of Manufacturing-segment revenue this quarter with no prior-year comparator -- the entire source of Group revenue growth, while legacy IT and Related Services (-8.5%) and Financial Services (-63.4%) segments both contracted.

Direct Cost growth (+33% YoY) outpaced revenue growth (+21%), compressing Group gross margin from 22.7% to 15.6% -- consistent with the newly-consolidated Manufacturing segment's different cost structure diluting the legacy IT/Financial Services margin mix.

Finance Cost +51% YoY (Rs.409.935mn vs Rs.271.085mn), plausibly linked to acquisition-related debt -- Group non-current interest-bearing borrowings rose from Rs.1,906.996mn (31 Mar 2026) to Rs.3,351.252mn (30 Jun 2026) within the quarter.
